dissents.topic: Severity of font-weight-notation HAS_NAMED matching inside font shorthand non-weight positions (font-family strings, url(), etc.)

positions.position: P0 — case-insensitive \b matches on 'normal', 'bold' etc. could fire inside font-family strings like 'Bold Sans' in the font shorthand, causing false skips. Invariant is unstated, TESTED-NOT-PROVED, would refuse in current form.
P1 — HAS_NAMED conflates lexical presence with semantic position; the regex doesn't know about shorthand position semantics. Wants tests covering ambiguous 'normal'/'bold' tokens in font shorthand.
P2 — flags \b boundary behavior on CSS values containing var() or hyphenated custom properties; wants confirmation via test but treats as lower risk.
P2 — notes pre-filters don't exclude string/comment contexts (e.g. 'bold' inside a font-family string) but treats as not a correctness bug, only a bound on the speedup.
Not flagged as a correctness concern — focuses on the /i flag asymmetry only.
Not flagged as a correctness concern — focuses on duplicated source of truth instead.

dissents.topic: Whether the missing benchmark numbers in a 'performance' PR is a blocker

positions.position: P1 — invokes his own rule: optimize the 3% that matters, only after measuring. Wants before/after timings on a representative corpus in the changeset.
P2 but called out forcefully — 'a perf patch without measurements is talk, not code'; requires benchmarks before landing.
P2 — 'don't tune for speed until you've measured'; wants at least one before/after number in the PR body.
Reframes as a correctness problem (P1) — 'performance is being fixed, but correctness is being asserted by silence'; the issue is missing tests of the invariant, not missing benchmarks.
P1 — calls it 'ugly' and 'the wrong shape'; wants either no filter passed or a branched walkRules call. walkRules with /./ still runs the regex test pointlessly.
P2 — a 'tell' that the data shape wants an optional filter; inconsistent with media-feature-range-notation two files over; wants uniform RegExp | undefined shape.
P2 — less readable sentinel; notes minor semantic edge that it would skip an empty selector where unfiltered form would not.
P2 — wants an invariant comment naming why /./ is safe rather than encoding it as a sentinel.

issues.description: font-weight-notation HAS_NAMED may false-skip in font shorthand where weight keywords appear inside font-family strings or unrelated positions
issues.detail: Case-insensitive \b on 'normal','bold','light','bolder' will also match inside font-family identifiers in the font shorthand (e.g., font: 12px/1 "Bold Sans";) and \d{3} can match line-height/size segments. The skip-precondition invariant — 'if regex misses, no diagnostic would have been produced' — is unstated and not test-locked. Dijkstra rates this as a refusal-blocking correctness gap; Hickey and Liskov flag the same surface at lower severity. Needs targeted tests for ambiguous shorthand cases plus an explicit invariant comment.

issues.description: Pre-filter regexes encode a load-bearing soundness invariant that is nowhere stated in code or tests
issues.detail: Every short-circuit assumes 'if the pre-filter regex does not match, the rule has nothing to report' — a superset/necessary-condition contract. No comment, spec, or test asserts it; if a future maintainer adds a new keyword to the rule without updating the regex, the rule silently stops reporting real violations. Multiple reviewers want a one-line contract comment above each HAS_* regex and tests exercising both branches of the short-circuit.

issues.description: keyframe-selector-notation HAS_PERCENTAGE lacks /i flag while HAS_KEYWORD has it; anchoring strategies also diverge
issues.detail: HAS_KEYWORD uses /i and \b; HAS_PERCENTAGE uses (?:^|[,\s]) and no /i. Selectors are case-insensitive in CSS so the asymmetry is at minimum a contract smell, and the divergent anchoring is intuited per-regex rather than derived from a single spec. Either unify or document why one side needs /i and the other doesn't.

issues.description: Performance PR ships with no cited benchmark numbers
issues.detail: The PR is titled 'Fix *-notation performance' but the description and changeset cite no before/after timings, corpus, or profile. Knuth invokes his measure-first rule; Torvalds calls perf-without-numbers 'talk, not code'; Pike notes that filters doing non-trivial regex work on every decl/at-rule could be a wash on inputs that don't trigger them. Attach hyperfine/internal benchmark output on a representative stylesheet.

issues.description: selector-pseudo-element-colon-notation: walkRules(/:/) replaces a named, commented guard with an opaque library affordance
issues.detail: The previous ruleNode.selector.includes(':') came with the comment 'get out early if no pseudo elements or classes'. The new walkRules(/:/, fn) is behavior-equivalent but the meaning is now invisible — control flow is governed by postcss's regex-as-selector-filter convention. Dijkstra calls this a SMUGGLED-GOTO via library affordance; Torvalds and Pike note the perf claim is oversold since /:/ matches almost every selector. Either restore the explicit guard or name the invariant in a comment.

issues.description: /./ sentinel regex used as 'match-anything' filter in keyframe-selector-notation is the wrong shape
issues.detail: The 'percentage-unless-within-keyword-only-block' branch sets selectorRegex = /./ so walkRules always fires. Torvalds calls it ugly and notes walkRules still runs the regex test per rule; Pike notes media-feature-range-notation two files over already uses the natural RegExp | undefined shape and the inconsistency is unjustified. Restructure so the filter-less walk is its own call (or pass undefined), and unify the pattern across the family of rules.

issues.description: Pre-filter pattern is duplicated across five+ rules without a shared abstraction; two sources of truth for keyword sets
issues.detail: HAS_NAMED, HAS_NUMERIC, HAS_PERCENTAGE, HAS_KEYWORD each reconstruct sets that already exist as data structures elsewhere; the same pre-filter shape appears in every *-notation rule. Pike flags this as a WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE smell — the regex shadows the keyword Set and both must change together. Hickey sees an emerging walkDeclsIf / walkIf helper. A small shared builder like buildKeywordRegex(set, flags) derived from the same source would eliminate the drift risk.

issues.description: media-feature-range-notation: 'prefix' guard /[<>]/ may miss bare '=' range syntax and other edges
issues.detail: Range notation in CSS is <, >, <=, >=, =. The [<>] filter catches <= and >= but a bare '=' (e.g., @media (width = 100px)) would be skipped. If that form is supposed to be flagged under primary='prefix', this is a missed-report regression. Dijkstra additionally notes /(?:min|max)-/i is correctly case-insensitive but the justifying invariant is unstated, and Torvalds notes it could match identifiers like --max-foo (false-positive only, so harmless).

issues.description: No new tests demonstrate the fast-path skip-precondition holds
issues.detail: Author claims a performance fix but adds no tests showing that for every input the original rule would have flagged, the new pre-filter does not skip. The changeset asserts performance; correctness is asserted by silence and reliance on the existing suite. Add boundary tests for cases that LOOK skippable but must not be (e.g., 'bold' inside font-family, var(--weight) in font shorthand, bare '=' in media range).

issues.description: font-weight-notation HAS_NAMED has /i flag but HAS_NUMERIC does not — asymmetric and undocumented
issues.detail: Harmless today because numeric weights are pure digits, but the asymmetry invites a future maintainer to add an alphabetic numeric synonym without thinking about case. A one-line '// digits only; no case flag needed' closes the loop.

issues.description: import-notation duplicates /url\(/i with inverted polarity across two adjacent branches
issues.detail: Two adjacent lines test the same regex with opposite polarity. Extract const hasUrl / const URL_FUNC, or write the policy as `if ((primary === 'string') !== hasUrl) return;` so the asymmetric polarity is named once and harder to invert by accident. Liskov also wants the underlying contract — 'rule reports iff params contain a notation different from primary' — stated explicitly.

issues.description: Six-rule change in a single patch — uniform but borderline for revertability
issues.detail: Touches six rules with the same shape of change; defensible because the pattern is uniform but a regression in any one requires reverting all. A maintainer could reasonably ask for one commit per rule. Flag for future PRs in the family.

issues.description: selector-not-notation switches from selector.includes(':not(') (case-sensitive) to /:not\(/i — undocumented behavior change
issues.detail: CSS pseudo-classes are case-insensitive per spec, so /i is arguably more correct, but it is a real behavior change for fixtures containing :NOT(. Worth a sentence in the changeset.
Will match identifiers like --max-foo. False positives only (slow path still produces correct output) so correctness is preserved, but \b(?:min|max)- would skip more cases cheaply.

issues.description: HAS_NUMERIC matches digit sequences anywhere including inside other tokens (e.g., rgb(400,…) or --weight-400)
issues.detail: Conservative over-approximation — falls through to the slow path on false positives, preserving correctness but bounding the speedup. Worth a comment that the filter is intentionally a coarse necessary condition.

issues.description: HAS_NAMED in font-weight-notation deduplicates two source arrays silently via Set
issues.detail: [...new Set([...fontWeightNonNumericKeywords, ...fontWeightRelativeKeywords])] is correct but obscures whether the two source arrays were expected to overlap. State the invariant or add a comment.

synthesis.summary: The panel broadly agrees the patch has the right shape — cheap regex pre-filters in front of expensive AST parsing across six *-notation rules — but converges on a structural critique: the fast-path encodes a load-bearing soundness invariant ('if the regex misses, the rule has nothing to report') that is nowhere stated, nowhere tested, and reconstructed in two places per rule (the regex and the parser-driven check). Knuth, Liskov, Dijkstra, and Pike all want this contract written down; Pike and Hickey additionally want a shared helper because the pattern is now duplicated five+ times. The strongest preserved disagreement is on font-weight-notation HAS_NAMED in the font shorthand: Dijkstra rates it P0/refuse-the-patch because 'Bold Sans' or var(--weight) cases plausibly defeat the invariant; Hickey rates it P1; Liskov and Knuth rate it P2; Torvalds and Pike don't flag it as a correctness concern at all. Secondary preserved disagreements: (1) whether missing benchmark numbers in a 'performance' PR is a blocker (Knuth/Torvalds/Pike say yes, Dijkstra reframes as a correctness-tests gap), and (2) whether the /./ sentinel regex is wrong-shape ugly (Torvalds P1, others P2 or quiet). Consensus minimum to land: add invariant comments to every pre-filter, add boundary tests for the look-skippable-but-aren't cases, fix the HAS_PERCENTAGE vs HAS_KEYWORD case/anchoring asymmetry in keyframe-selector-notation, replace the /./ sentinel with a uniform optional-filter shape, and attach before/after benchmark numbers to the changeset.
